summary: Context Guardian observes the existing SQLite logical-session owner without Node CLI.
reason: Historic main-only scope and cron/direct kind kept; contextTokens now follows the installed CLI rule (trusted stored window, else 200000), proven line by line against the historical command on 87 real main rows (#131): identical contextTokens/totalTokens/kind and 3 soft / 3 hard.

tests.name: Context Guardian SQLite read-only owner contracts
tests.evidence: 13 SQLite/shell tests: real STRICT schema and PR82 rows; parity with `openclaw sessions --json --limit all` on the 87 joined real main rows of s24-2026-10-11b/c8 (contextTokens, totalTokens, kind, 3 soft / 3 hard); trusted-window rule cases; main-only scope over 937 rows; WAL RO, 200001-row bound, atomic 0600, prior-health preservation.

capabilities.reason: NO_CAPABILITY: existing internal Guardian observation, no app/agent/voice route.

architecture.reason: Existing Guardian lock, periodic cycle and private health snapshot reused; no new store, scheduler, daemon or projection configuration owner.

mcp_owner_parity.reason: Native facade only; canonical MCP admission and dispatch contracts unchanged.

rollback: Revert the Guardian reader delta; no runtime deployment performed.
limitations: Physical Guardian after-measurement remains Claude's recette (before: CLI 9659 ms on 10/10, 2912 ms on 11/10).
The port assumes the catalog lookups resolve nothing, as observed on OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (87/87 rows at 200000); after an OpenClaw upgrade the CLI/SQLite join must be redone.
Scope is main only, no active window; other agent stores are deliberately ignored, matching the historical command.
Bound 10000 sessions refuses overflow; SQLite WAL SHM reader coordination may change while logical DB/WAL data stays unchanged.
